faq.a: Polarised light is light whose waves all wiggle in one direction. Ordinary sunlight wiggles in all directions, but reflection from water or glass makes it partly polarised.
The lenses have a filter that lets through only light wiggling up and down. Glare reflected from flat surfaces wiggles mostly side to side, so the filter blocks most of it.
Glare is bright sunlight reflected from flat, shiny surfaces like water, wet roads, snow or car windows. It can dazzle you and hide what is underneath.
asks: Why is the sea so bright to look at?

faq.q: Why does glare come back when I tilt my head?
faq.a: Tilting turns the filter so it now lets side-to-side light through, which is exactly the glare. Turning back blocks it again, a simple test for polarised lenses.
asks: How can I tell if sunglasses are polarised?
Why do polarised glasses stop working sideways?

faq.a: Yes. Bees and ants can see the pattern of polarised light in the blue sky and use it like a compass, even when the Sun is hidden behind a cloud.
asks: How do bees use polarised light?

facts: Sunlight reflected from water is partly polarised, mostly horizontally, and is most strongly polarised at about 53 degrees from straight down.
Bees and ants use the polarisation pattern of the blue sky to navigate.

quiz.say: You wear polarised sunglasses by a lake and tilt your head sideways. What happens to the glare on the water?
quiz.show: Tilting polarised glasses 90 degrees makes the glare…
quiz.why: Tilting turns the filter so it lets side-to-side light through, which is the polarised glare.

wrong.0: The filter only blocks glare when it is the right way round.
wrong.2: Polarising filters do not change the colour of the light.
